eligibility.quote:
This problem is due to the combination of new qt_gui_core packages with "old" rqt packages.
I committed changes to both repos, but only the qt_gui_core was tagged and released, the latest tag on the rqt repo is 3 month old...
eligibility.reason: The separately released Python plugin provider and GUI framework disagree on the descriptor interface. This is an UPGRADE interaction, not merely dependency installation or an absent icon file.

failed_conditions.reason: Both dictionary-key accessors identify the rename. The issue's printed Python descriptor dictionaries still contain plugin_path, whereas package_path is present only for the C++ plugins shown.

detection_stage.reason: The framework raises the diagnostic during startup plugin discovery/menu construction, before normal plugin operation: activate.

resolution.quote:
Just dropped down the latest source for qt_gui_core and rqt and recompiled kobuki_qtestsuite against them with relative icons.

All seems ok :+1:!
resolution.reason: This is an actual joint test of the two selected repositories, not just a merge. Historical groovy-devel commit queries through 2013-06-03 independently returned ffae1f756dbf23194a2628922939d9633df947f6 and 9682b9af78eecd368004fe7596e341eb84abc719, consistent with the specified latest-source pair. The SHA attribution is inferred, not explicitly printed by the tester.

notes: Read both issue threads and the original and final fixing diffs. Read historical head metadata via https://api.github.com/repos/ros-visualization/qt_gui_core/commits?sha=groovy-devel&until=2013-06-03T23:59:59Z&per_page=1 and the corresponding rqt endpoint. Their commit messages were 'make plugin resources relative to plugin.xml, fix help provider (#16)' and 'make plugin resources relative to plugin.xml (ros-visualization/qt_gui_core#16)'. The interim rollback and opposite old/new pairing are not the selected resolved pair. The plugin-relative versus package-relative XML discussion concerns an additional plugin/framework pairing, not another established condition in the originally broken descriptor pair.
